identity.name: Endeavour Perpetual Calendar
identity.one_liner: The Moser Perpetual Calendar — the watch that proved H. Moser could compete at the haute horlogerie price point, with a fumé dial, an HMC 341 caliber, and a no-logo design philosophy.

narrative.story: The Endeavour Perpetual Calendar is the 2015 reference that established H. Moser as a haute horlogerie brand. The HMC 341 caliber is a manual-wind perpetual calendar with a 7-day reserve, an interchangeable escapement module, and a small seconds. The dial is a fumé smoked salmon or green, with no logo — Moser's deliberate "no logo" statement. The Perpetual Calendar is the most-cited Moser of the 2010s, and the watch that has been compared to the Patek 5140 in the value-per-dollar argument.
narrative.collector_notes: The 2018 Endeavour Perpetual Calendar in steel was the first Moser in steel at the haute horlogerie price point, a deliberate move to make the brand accessible to the Royal Oak / Nautilus buyer who wanted a different design language.
